stances.claim: Duterte remains a 'national enigma' despite 25 years in political office because his circle of friends is limited to Davao City and San Beda College -- making the Bedan network the most analytically tractable window into who he is and how he governs.

Duterte's testimonial reception persona -- informal, self-deprecating ('just an average student in San Beda'), generous in crediting Ramos for persuading him to run, ventriloquist mimic of his 'terror-professor' Justice Arsenio Solidum, eating monggo soup and banana maruya -- is irreconcilable with the public 'strongman' image; the Bedan setting reveals a softer, conversational Duterte that the public rarely sees.
stances.rhetorical_move: private-vs-public persona contrast (informal Duterte ≠ strongman Duterte)

stances.claim: Bedan Cabinet appointees Medialdea (Executive Office), Aguirre (Justice), Tugade (Transportation), Salalima (DICT), and Lim (Pagcor), plus cited Bedans Robles, Brillantes, Cruz, and Acosta -- alongside non-Bedan close associates Carlos Dominguez (kindergarten-to-HS valedictorian-classmate), Panelo, Yasay (YMCA dorm buddy), and Domingo -- represent the institutional infrastructure of Duterte governance and merit close watching.

Bedan critics -- Sen. Leila de Lima (Law 1985) lambasting 'daily executions' in the drug war ('the day has already come when we can no longer tell who is morally wrong among us: the nine-year-old street child sniffing rugby, or the policeman who shoots the child in the head') and former Sen. Rene Saguisag (frail but acerbic on Duterte's dynasty, Quiboloy gifts, undisclosed bank accounts) -- represent the Bedan-internal counterweight that legitimizes critique from within the President's home network.
stances.rhetorical_move: internal-network critique amplification (Bedan critics carry special weight against Bedan president)

stances.claim: Despite Bedan dominance of the government, the nation is 'safe in their hands as long as among them are pros and contras, supporters and dissenters, admirers and critics' -- making intra-network pluralism the saving structural feature, not the network itself.
stances.rhetorical_move: pluralism-as-safeguard framing (heterogeneity within network as protective feature)
stances.confidence: asserted as the column's organizing verdict

notable_anecdotes: Duterte's testimonial reception persona -- eating monggo soup and fried banana maruya, conversing softly with table friends, taking selfies with alumni 'to the obvious discomfort of his security men' -- the column's most humanizing portrait of the President.

The ventriloquist mimicry of CA Justice Arsenio Solidum's 'stentorian and raspy voice,' Duterte miming his late mentor's 'booming questions and his own uncharacteristically meek answers' -- the moment that 'brought the house down' and that CJ 'easily identified with' because Solidum was also CJ's 'terror-professor' at FEU.

Duterte's first-of-records joke preserved verbatim: 'I established a record of sorts as the first mayor to be president, the first Mindanaoan to be president, and the first president to be inaugurated with two first families in attendance!' -- a rare unfiltered Duterte joke about himself.

The Ramos-Dureza-Dominguez Davao persuasion trip recounted: 'a probinsyano who did not know his way around the corridors of power,' he 'confessed to having no presidential ambition at all. But Ramos was insistent, and he could no longer resist' -- humanizing Duterte's path to presidency as accidental rather than ambitious.

De Lima's quoted maiden privilege speech: 'The day has already come when we can no longer tell who is morally wrong among us: the nine-year-old street child sniffing rugby, or the policeman who shoots the child in the head for sniffing rugby. This is our descent as a nation into the darkness that these men have created for us.' -- the column's most rhetorically charged single passage from any politician.

Saguisag's acerbic catalog: 'The Dutertes may reign forever. Prez, Mayor, Vice Mayor... PD No. 46 punishes giver and recipient who accepts gifts. Whose aircraft is Digong using? The allegedly simple man accepts a Safari and Expedition from Pastor Quiboloy. He does not disclose the family bank account, which, Trillanes alleges, reaches billions. No transparency.' -- itemizing the substantive critique without CJ adopting it.
CJ's parallel-identification anchor: Justice Solidum was also CJ's 'terror-professor' at FEU -- using shared educational trauma to authenticate the column's intimate observational stance.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban attempts to decode President Duterte through his Bedan (San Beda College) network -- noting that despite Duterte's 25-year political career (mayor, vice mayor, congressman), his circle of friends remains limited to Davao City and San Beda, making the Bedan network the most analytically tractable window into his governance. At a recent SBLAA testimonial reception, CJ (as honorary SBLAA member since 2006) was seated within conversational distance of Duterte at the head table, alongside the only other honorary member, former President Fidel V. Ramos. The informal gathering -- rowdy guffaws, selfies discomforting his security men, monggo soup and fried banana maruya -- revealed a softer Duterte who set aside his prepared speech for heart-to-heart conversation. He generously credited Ramos (with Dureza and Dominguez) for persuading him to run despite his self-description as 'a probinsyano who did not know his way around the corridors of power' with 'no presidential ambition at all.' Self-deprecatingly calling himself 'just an average student in San Beda,' he cited his Bedan Cabinet -- Salvador Medialdea (Executive Office), Vitaliano Aguirre (Justice), Arthur Tugade (Transportation), Rodolfo Salalima (DICT), and Alfredo Lim (Pagcor) -- plus other Bedans not yet in government: Rodolfo Robles (bar topnotcher, his former professor), Sixto Brillantes (former Comelec chair), Avelino V. Cruz (bar topnotcher, former professor, SBLAA chair), and CA Justice Francisco Acosta (SBLAA president); he also praised non-Bedan close associates Carlos Dominguez (his kindergarten-to-HS valedictorian-classmate), Salvador Panelo, Perfecto Yasay Jr. (his YMCA dorm buddy), and Andrea Domingo. Duterte joked about being the first mayor, first Mindanaoan, and first president inaugurated with two first families in attendance; what brought the house down was his ventriloquist-like imitation of CA Justice Arsenio Solidum's stentorian and raspy voice -- his late 'terror-professor,' whom CJ also identifies as his own 'terror-professor' at FEU. CJ notes other Bedan SC Justices Bienvenido L. Reyes (who administered Duterte's oath) and Jose C. Mendoza, plus VP Leni Robredo's San Beda graduate studies. But the column's counterweight is Bedan critics conspicuously absent from the testimonial: Sen. Leila de Lima (Law 1985), the first legislator to lambast the 'daily executions' in the drug war, whose maiden privilege speech mourned 'The day has already come when we can no longer tell who is morally wrong among us: the nine-year-old street child sniffing rugby, or the policeman who shoots the child in the head for sniffing rugby. This is our descent as a nation into the darkness that these men have created for us' and called for a congressional inquiry on extrajudicial killings; and former Senator Rene Saguisag (now frail but acerbically penning): 'The Dutertes may reign forever. Prez, Mayor, Vice Mayor... PD No. 46 punishes giver and recipient who accepts gifts. Whose aircraft is Digong using? The allegedly simple man accepts a Safari and Expedition from Pastor Quiboloy. He does not disclose the family bank account, which, Trillanes alleges, reaches billions. No transparency.' CJ concludes: 'Like it or not, our government is now dominated by Bedans all. But I think the nation is safe in their hands as long as among them are pros and contras, supporters and dissenters, admirers and critics.'
